topic: correcting gaps or overlaps when measuring with same-size units
subtitle: Laying units with no gaps or overlaps, spotting a gap or overlap mistake, and fixing the count

traps.desc: reported the number of cubes counted, but the cubes overlapped so two extra cubes were squeezed onto the ribbon
put the two counts together instead of finding how many more
added the two numbers instead of finding how many cubes the gaps hid

problems.desc: Open response. Rex overlapped his cubes and counted 10; Ivy laid hers end to end with no gaps or overlaps and counted 8. Rex claims his bigger number means his measurement is better. The child must say Rex is wrong and explain that overlapping lets extra cubes fit, so a bigger count can come from a sloppy lay-down, not a longer ribbon. Read the drawing and the reasoning, not just the word yes or no.
